stated_evidence.behavioral_claim: The production encoder sizes a conservative ordinary reply: 256 actions and disposition entries in eight phases, 512 retained validator records with each bounded scalar and raw line maximized, up to 768 association issues, per-phase diagnostics, and maximal profile capture. Separately encoded declaration/issuer, lifecycle-event, fresh-read, fresh-write, exec-observation and actor components are added without reclaiming ordinary fields. Actor components use the union of encoded success, failure, interruption and capture fixtures: eight actor records with full compiled-profile payloads, sixteen phase overheads, every event, transfer and resource at its capacity, aggregate disposition entries and issues, and ordinary-step actor identities. Bounded echoed strings use maximal escaping, native scalars use 20 decimal bytes, fixed actor vocabulary has a checked 128-byte ASCII ceiling, and each array has an explicit capacity. The actor capture allowance is compared with production encoding of a maximum receipt; missing capture fixtures and unclassified or oversized arrays fail. Ordinary controls separately encode valid exec evidence and fresh-write evidence on every slot. Mutually exclusive fields remain counted, so this is an upper bound, not a reachable reply. Every string key across all reply-shape documents must have a size policy. Real transport controls separately measure admitted ordinary, fresh-read, fresh-write, mixed native and actor capture workloads.
